sources.locator: ch. 3 §§3.1-3.3, printed pp. 6-8 (Hilbert and Riesz transforms, homogeneous SIOs, Calderon-Zygmund kernels and operators); ch. 7 §§7.1-7.2 and 7.6-7.7, printed pp. 29-33 and 40-47 (BMO, John-Nirenberg, the SIO mapping property, atoms, H1-BMO duality). Proofs of Theorem 7.5, Proposition 7.6, Proposition 7.7, Proposition 7.35, Theorem 7.40 and Definition 7.39 were read in full.

contents.name: §3.1 Hilbert and Riesz transforms: Hf = pi^{-1} p.v. int f(y)/(x-y) dy, the Riesz kernels c_n x_j/|x|^{n+1}, and homogeneous singular integral operators
contents.proof_mapping: the local lemma reconstructs the operator-kernel off-support representation for the two classical kernels from the published FR-7 principal-value and adjointness items

contents.name: §§3.2-3.4 homogeneous SIOs are weak (1,1) and strong (p,p) for 1<p<infinity, and the Calderon-Zygmund decomposition proof strategy
contents.reason: the strict-range Lp mapping theory of the Hilbert and Riesz transforms is owned by the published FR-7 and FR-8 pages of this track; this page consumes only the endpoint L-infinity to BMO statement

contents.name: Definition 3.1 (Calderon-Zygmund kernels: pointwise size, Hormander's condition, cancellation; CZ operator as a principal-value limit) with Remark 3.2 (L2 extension by density; Tf=W*f for Schwartz f)
contents.reason: the library's published Calderon-Zygmund convention is the annular-size plus Hormander plus off-support-representation definition; W's complementary principal-value formulation is corroborative and is not adopted as this page's contract

contents.name: Definition 7.1(a) the sharp maximal function f-sharp
contents.reason: the duality proof works with the local mean oscillation directly and never with the sharp maximal function; maximal-oscillation characterisations belong to the planned weighted and Littlewood-Paley material

contents.name: Definition 7.1(b) the BMO seminorm sup_Q Av_Q|f-f_Q|
Proposition 7.2 (f-sharp-sharp is comparable to f-sharp)
contents.reason: the comparison of the sharp maximal functions taken over cubes versus over constants is not needed; the definition item records only the optimal-constant identity that the page uses

contents.name: Example 7.3 (log|x| is in BMO)
Lemma 7.4 (nested cubes with halving side lengths: |f_{Q_n}-f_{Q_0}| <= 2dn |f|_BMO)
Theorem 7.5 (John-Nirenberg inequality, with the constants normalised by |f|_BMO)
Proposition 7.6 and (7.10) (all finite Lp oscillation norms are bounded by the BMO seminorm)
Proposition 7.7 and (7.11) (the SIO mapping property |Tf|_BMO <= C B |f|_infinity for f in L-infinity ∩ L2)

Definition 7.8, Remark 7.9, Proposition 7.10 (good-lambda inequality), Remarks 7.11-7.12, Proposition 7.13 (comparison of the dyadic maximal function with f-sharp) and Proposition 7.14 (interpolation property of BMO)
contents.reason: the dyadic maximal function and BMO interpolation block belongs to the Littlewood-Paley and interpolation pages of the track; this page proves no interpolation theorem and uses the cube maximal function only through already published items

contents.name: §7.3 (Haar functions and dyadic harmonic analysis), Remark 7.15, Theorem 7.16, Definition 7.17, Remark 7.18, Theorem 7.19 (Littlewood-Paley for the dyadic square function) and Remark 7.20
contents.reason: the dyadic Haar and square-function development is the subject of the planned Littlewood-Paley page and is not consumed by any item of this page

contents.name: §7.4 (dyadic H1 - dyadic BMO duality): Definition 7.21, Proposition 7.22 (Carleson condition), Remark 7.23, Definition 7.24, Proposition 7.25, Theorem 7.26 (atomic decomposition), Remark 7.27, Proposition 7.28 (Fefferman's inequality) and Proposition 7.29 (BMO = (H1)*)
contents.reason: the [0,1] dyadic warm-up is not adopted: the page proves the classical cube-based duality from the published real-Hardy-space suppliers, and the one-grid distinction is recorded separately on the examples page

contents.name: §7.6 Proposition 7.30 (Riesz-transform and Poisson-maximal forms of the H1 characterisation) with Definition 7.31 (nontangential cones) and Proposition 7.32
contents.reason: the radial, nontangential and grand maximal characterisations and the Riesz-transform form are owned by the in-run FR-9 page, which supplies the maximal objects and atom machinery this page consumes

contents.name: §7.6 the square-function form of Proposition 7.30
contents.reason: the square-function characterisation of H1 is the subject of the planned FR-11 Littlewood-Paley page of this run and is not consumed by any FR-10 item

contents.name: Remark 7.33 (density of nice classes in H1, completeness of H1, continuity of the injection into S')
contents.proof_mapping: the embeddability of mean-zero L2 functions on a cube is proved locally from the FR-9 maximal machinery rather than cited; the completeness and density statements are not consumed

contents.name: Definition 7.34 (L2 atoms) and Proposition 7.35 (every L2 atom has H1 norm at most a dimensional constant)
Proposition 7.36 (atomic decomposition of H1), Remark 7.37 and Proposition 7.38 (the R-based special case)
contents.reason: the classical atomic decomposition is the central theorem of the in-run FR-9 page, which is the supplier of the atom definition, the coefficient bound and the density of finite atomic sums used here

contents.name: Definition 7.39 (the action of b in BMO on H1: the atom pairing, the truncation argument and the weak-star limit)
Theorem 7.40 ((H1)* = BMO: the canonical map, injectivity, the Riesz-representation construction and the norm bounds)

contents.name: Examples 3.5(1) (L-infinity is contained in BMO with seminorm at most twice the sup norm)

contents.name: Theorem 3.8 (BMO modulo constants is a Banach space)
contents.reason: completeness of BMO is not used: the duality theorem's compactness input is Banach-Alaoglu in the dual of H1, and no argument on this page takes limits in the BMO norm

contents.name: Example 3.14 (explicit distribution function of log|x| on an interval)

contents.name: Theorem 3.15 (John-Nirenberg via a recursive Calderon-Zygmund decomposition)

contents.reason: the page records one standard form of the exponential bound; sharp constants and alternative proofs are not used by any item

contents.name: Theorem 3.28 (equivalence of the Lq oscillation seminorms) with Remark 3.29 (BMO is contained in Lp_loc for every finite p)
Theorem 3.30 (local exponential integrability of BMO functions)
contents.reason: the exponential-integrability form is a corollary of the distribution-function bound recorded here and is consumed by no item on this page
